title: The 7 Best Sunsama Alternatives for 2026
summary: Want Sunsama alternatives that cost less or do more of the work for you? We compared 7 daily planners so you can pick the right fit for your day.
body_markdown:
Most people searching for Sunsama alternatives aren't unhappy with the idea behind it. Sunsama gets something important right: a good day starts with a realistic plan, and a good evening ends with a clean shutdown.


The trouble is everything around that idea. At $17 to $22 a month, it's one of the pricier planners out there. The daily ritual can take 10 to 15 minutes, and on a chaotic day it's the first thing to go. And every task still has to be pulled in, sorted and sized by you.


So what should you use instead? That depends on which part of Sunsama wore you down.


We picked seven planners that each fix a different part of it.


## Key takeaways


-


**BOND** is the best Sunsama alternative for executives who don't have time for a daily ritual. It builds and prioritizes your to-do list from email, Slack and meetings.


-


**Akiflow** and **Morgen** keep the planning-first approach with more speed or more AI help.


-


**Structured** , **TickTick** and **Todoist** are the lowest-cost options if price was the dealbreaker.


## The quick list


1.


**BOND** : your priorities, ready before you open your laptop.


2.


**Akiflow** : Sunsama's task inbox and time blocking, built for speed.


3.


**Morgen** : an AI planner that drafts your day for you to approve.


4.


**Motion** : hands the whole scheduling job to AI.


5.


**Structured** : a visual daily timeline with a generous free plan.


6.


**TickTick** : lists, calendar, focus timer and habits for under $5 a month.


7.


**Todoist** : a fast, dependable list with light AI features.


## Why people look for Sunsama alternatives


A few reasons come up again and again:


-


**Cost.** Pro is $17/month billed yearly or $22 billed monthly. For a solo user just building a planning habit, that's a lot.


-


**The ritual takes time.** The guided morning plan is the point of Sunsama, but it's also the first thing skipped when your day starts with a fire.


-


**Manual triage.** Sunsama shows you tasks from your tools, but you still decide what's a task, what matters and how long it takes.


-


**Time-boxing can feel heavy.** When the day goes sideways, a carefully timed plan falls apart.


If you're a busy leader, the third point is the big one. Your work doesn't arrive as neat tasks. It arrives as emails, Slack threads and meeting notes. Sorting all of that every morning is the job you wanted help with in the first place.


## How we picked


We looked for tools that fix at least one of those problems, then compared them on:


-


**Daily effort** : how much time it takes to keep the plan useful


-


**How tasks get in** : typed, synced or found automatically


-


**Who sets priorities** : you, rules or AI


-


**Price** : checked on each vendor's pricing page or app store listing in October 2026


## 1. BOND


*Your to-do list on autopilot.*


BOND takes the part of Sunsama that eats your morning—gathering and sorting tasks—and does it for you. It connects to Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion and your other tools, finds the commitments hiding in them, and turns them into a single to-do list ranked P0 to P3. The list updates on its own as your day changes.


Instead of a planning ritual, you get a morning brief: what needs your attention, who's waiting on you, and what's coming up. BOND learns your priorities as you go, so the brief gets sharper over time. Users describe it as cutting through the noise, which is exactly what a ritual is supposed to do, minus the 15 minutes.


**Key features**


-


Self-updating to-do list built from your email, Slack, calendar and docs


-


Tracks commitments and what others owe you


-


Meeting briefs and follow-up drafts in your voice


-


Works where you already are, in Slack and iMessage


-


Routines for weekly and monthly recurring work


**What works:** You get Sunsama's clarity without the daily upkeep. Because BOND reads the source of each task, its priorities are extremely accurate, and nothing slips because you forgot to drag it in.


**Limitations:** There's no guided shutdown ritual, so if you love that part of Sunsama, you'll miss it. It's built for work rather than personal planning, and at $49/month it costs more than Sunsama.


**Pricing:** Free to start with 10,000 credits. Individual plan is $49/month. Enterprise is custom.


**Best for:** Executives and chiefs of staff whose days are too reactive for a fixed morning ritual. It works a lot like an AI chief of staff, and for more on that kind of role, see what a chief of staff actually does.


## 2. Akiflow


*Prioritizes speed.*


Akiflow is the most direct Sunsama replacement here. It pulls tasks from your tools into one inbox, lets you drag them onto your calendar and supports a daily planning routine. The difference is speed. Almost everything has a keyboard shortcut, and the AI assistant, Aki, can help plan through chat.


**What works:** If you like Sunsama's model but find it slow, Akiflow feels like an upgrade.


**Limitations:** It's no cheaper on a monthly plan, there's no free tier, and you still do the triage yourself. The AI meeting assistant costs an extra $19/month.


**Pricing:** Pro is $19/month billed yearly or $34 monthly. 7-day trial (card required).


**Best for:** Keyboard-first users who want Sunsama's workflow at full speed.


## 3. Morgen


*An AI first draft of your day.*


Morgen keeps the "plan your day" mindset but lets AI do the first pass. Its AI Planner looks at your tasks, calendar and priorities and proposes a time-blocked day. You adjust it and confirm.


It brings calendars and tasks from tools like Todoist, Notion and ClickUp into one view, and runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, mobile and the web.


**What works:** A shorter planning routine than Sunsama, with you still in charge. The yearly price is lower too.


**Limitations:** Better as a planning layer than a full task manager. Monthly billing is twice the yearly rate.


**Pricing:** $15/month billed yearly or $30 monthly for individuals. Teams pay $10/seat/month yearly or $25 monthly. 14-day free trial, no card needed.


**Best for:** Sunsama users who want the ritual to take two minutes instead of fifteen.


## 4. Motion


*Let AI do the planning entirely.*


Motion goes all the way. Give it tasks with deadlines and priorities, and it schedules your calendar for you, reshuffling whenever plans change. It has also grown into a broader work platform with projects, docs and meeting tools.


**What works:** No daily planning at all. Motion handles it continuously.


**Limitations:** It's the opposite of Sunsama's mindful approach, which some people find stressful. Every task still needs to be entered, and it's not cheap.


**Pricing:** Pro AI from $19/seat/month and Business AI from $29/seat/month, with a free trial.


**Best for:** People who want to stop planning altogether. (If you're curious what else is out there, we compared the best Motion alternatives too.)


## 5. Structured


*A visual timeline for your day, free to start.*


Structured lays your day out as a single colorful timeline, mixing tasks, events and routines. It's simple, pleasant to use, and has a built-in focus timer plus AI help for building a plan. With over 15 million downloads, it's one of the most popular daily planners around.


**What works:** It captures the calm, one-day-at-a-time feel of Sunsama for far less money.


**Limitations:** It's designed for personal planning. There are fewer work integrations than Sunsama, and no team features.


**Pricing:** Free plan available. Pro is sold in the app, as a subscription or a lifetime purchase. Structured doesn't publish prices on its website, so check its App Store or Google Play listing.


**Best for:** Individuals who want a visual daily plan on a budget.


## 6. TickTick


*All-in-one planning for cheap.*


TickTick combines task lists, calendar views, a Pomodoro timer and a habit tracker in one app. You can plan your day in its calendar view much as you would in Sunsama, just without the guided steps.


**What works:** Premium costs $49.99 a year, less than three months of Sunsama.


**Limitations:** Prioritization is manual and its AI features are light. The free plan caps you at 9 lists.


**Pricing:** Free plan available. Premium is $49.99/year.


**Best for:** Budget-conscious planners who want lots of features in one place.


## 7. Todoist


*A great list, no ritual required.*


Todoist is for people who realized they don't need a daily planning ceremony, just a list they trust. Natural language input makes adding tasks fast, and features like Ramble turn spoken thoughts into tasks.


**What works:** It's quick, stable and works on every platform.


**Limitations:** No built-in daily planning flow, and you set every priority yourself.


**Pricing:** Free plan available. Pro is $5/month billed yearly ($7 monthly). Business is $8/user/month yearly ($10 monthly).


**Best for:** People who want simplicity over structure.


## Which Sunsama alternative is right for you?


Start with what pushed you away.


**"I don't have time to plan every morning."** BOND does the sorting and prioritizing for you, so you start the day already knowing what matters. Morgen is the middle ground if you still want to approve a plan.


**"It's too expensive."** Structured, TickTick and Todoist all have free plans and cheap upgrades.


**"It's too slow."** Akiflow keeps the same model with much faster controls.


**"I want AI to plan for me."** Motion schedules everything automatically.


Still not sure how to decide what matters most each day? For a wider look at AI planners, see our list of the best AI to-do list apps. Our guide on how to prioritize tasks when everything is P0 is a good place to start. And if you're looking for broader help than a planner, see our roundup of the best AI executive assistants.


## FAQ


**What are the best Sunsama alternatives?**


For executives and busy leaders, BOND is the top pick because it builds and prioritizes your to-do list automatically, without a daily ritual. If you want a near-identical workflow, Akiflow is the closest match.


**Is there a free alternative to Sunsama?**


Yes. Structured, TickTick and Todoist all have free plans. BOND offers 10,000 free credits to start, and Morgen has a 14-day free trial.


**Is there a cheaper Sunsama alternative?**


TickTick Premium is $49.99 a year and Todoist Pro is $5/month billed yearly. Morgen is $15/month billed yearly, just under Sunsama's $17.


**Does Sunsama use AI?**


Sunsama's paid plan includes AI and MCP support, but its core approach is a manual, guided planning routine. If you want AI to do more of the work, look at BOND, Morgen or Motion.


**What's the difference between Sunsama and Motion?**


Sunsama helps you plan your day yourself through a guided ritual. Motion plans it for you by auto-scheduling tasks onto your calendar. Morgen sits in between.


**Can I use a Sunsama alternative with Google Calendar?**


Yes. Akiflow, Morgen, Motion, TickTick and Todoist all connect to Google Calendar, and BOND reads your calendar to understand your meetings and commitments.
